channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Vieira se reúne com embaixador da Argentina e repudia falas de Milei
item.description: The Brazilian government summoned Argentina's ambassador to Brazil, Daniel Raimondi, to convey its repudiation of statements made by Argentine President Javier Milei, who called Minister Alexandre de Moraes a 'bald trash' during a PL event in São Paulo. Brazil also recalled its own ambassador to Argentina, Júlio Bitelli, for consultations—a diplomatic move indicating greater seriousness. The developments followed Milei's participation in the PL convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy.

item.title: Novo oficializa candidatura de Romeu Zema sem indicação de vice
item.description: The Novo party officially launched Romeu Zema's presidential candidacy at a convention in Brasília on Monday, the 27th. Zema has not yet chosen a running mate, though former STF justice Joaquim Barbosa is being considered for the vice-presidential slot. Zema plans to meet with Barbosa soon. Novo president João Caldas said he does not oppose the pairing and called it a 'great ticket'.

item.title: PSB espera até 3ª feira definição de Josué sobre vice do PT em MG
item.description: The PSB expects to decide by Tuesday (July 28, 2026) whether Josué Gomes, former Fiesp president and son of José Alencar, will be the vice-presidential candidate on Patrus Ananias’s (PT) ticket for Minas Gerais governor. The decision hinges on internal discussions and potential direct involvement from Lula, who supports the alliance. The PSB also considers Jarbas Soares Júnior as an alternative for vice or Senate, maintaining the strategy of a majoritarian coalition with the PT.

item.title: O show de Milei
item.description: Javier Milei's diatribes against Lula and Alexandre de Moraes are disproportionate and reveal the triumph of the Argentine president's ego over his country's interests. His irrational rhetoric makes rational analysis difficult and harms bilateral relations.

item.title: Flávio tem 57% contra 34% de Lula no 2º turno no Acre, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data survey released on July 27, 2026, shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 57% against 34% for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in a hypothetical presidential runoff in Acre. In the first-round scenario, Flávio also leads with 50% versus Lula’s 30%. The poll surveyed 1,600 people from July 22–25, has a 2-point margin of error, and is registered with the TSE under BR-08086/2026.

item.title: Crusoé: Flávio ganha um trono, mas não um reino
item.description: The Liberal Party (PL) convention in São Paulo was designed to establish Flávio Bolsonaro’s hegemony within the bolsonarist movement, symbolically placing him center stage alongside his wife, Fernanda. Despite the institutional backing and visibility, the event did not secure him full control of the movement, revealing internal divisions and resistance from other bolsonarist leaders.

item.title: Maioria diz que família, amigos, imprensa e redes sociais não influenciam voto, aponta Datafolha
item.description: A majority of Brazilians state that the opinions of family, friends, journalists, social media influencers, and religious leaders will not influence their choice of presidential candidate in the 2026 elections, according to a Datafolha poll released on July 27, 2026.

item.title: Novo oficializa a candidatura de Romeu Zema à Presidência da República
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) officially launched his presidential candidacy at the party's national convention in Brasília, attended by party president Eduardo Ribeiro. Despite not yet announcing a running mate, Zema cited a BTG/Nexus poll showing him technically tied with Lula in a potential second-round runoff (42% to 46%). He positioned himself as a champion of right-wing economic liberalism, citing his Minas Gerais administration as a national model and mentioning Michelle Bolsonaro as a possible vice-presidential pick — which she has denied.

item.title: Durigan diz que próximo governo deve detalhar corte de gastos este ano
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that the next government, whether continuity or not, must present, still in 2026 after the elections, the details of a spending cut to begin in 2027, focused on mandatory expenditures. He emphasized the need for a fiscal adjustment of 2 percentage points of GDP on spending to bring public debt down, while advocating for greater efficiency and room for structural investments. Durigan also suggested that the STF act as a moderator of 'budget-bomb' proposals in Congress, which increase fixed spending without financing sources.

item.title: Lula recebe presidente sul-coreano para ampliar comércio
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung was received by Lula at the Palácio da Alvorada with full state honors, signaling a deepening of bilateral ties. The visit includes discussions on trade, technology, defense, and a potential Mercosul-South Korea free trade agreement, with emphasis on semiconductors, critical minerals, and energy transition.

item.title: Crise com Argentina: Embaixador chega a Brasília; conversa com Vieira ocorre até 4ª
item.description: Brazil's ambassador to Argentina, Julio Bitelli, returned to Brasília after being recalled by Itamaraty in protest over Argentine President Javier Milei's insults toward President Lula and Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. Bitelli is expected to meet with Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira by Wednesday, though a detailed talk may be delayed due to Vieira's schedule, including a meeting with South Korea's president and a trip to Peru. Argentina's ambassador in Brazil was also summoned for explanations, worsening bilateral tensions that have persisted since Milei took office.

item.title: Zema chega à convenção sem vice e com candidatura pouco competitiva
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) was officially announced as the presidential candidate at a convention in Brasília, but without a running mate and limited support from major parties. He trails behind leaders Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro in voter intentions, and stated the vice-presidential pick will be decided later, possibly through an alliance with Podemos or a Novo-only ticket. Zema reiterated he will not be Bolsonaro’s running mate and will stay in the race until the end.

item.title: Sem vice, Novo confirma Zema à Presidência da República
item.description: The Novo Party officially nominated former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema as its presidential candidate at a national convention in Brasília, with no running mate yet named. Zema emphasized his private-sector background, criticized the Supreme Federal Court and the Lula government, claiming he possesses the credentials to win, while party president Eduardo Ribeiro praised Zema’s Minas Gerais administration as a model to defeat the PT nationally.

item.title: Ministro das Relações Exteriores se reúne com embaixador da Argentina e transmite repúdio sobre declarações de Milei sobre Lula
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira met with Argentina's ambassador to Brazil, Daniel Raimondi, to convey the Brazilian government's repudiation of statements made by Argentine President Javier Milei during his visit to São Paulo, in which he attacked President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, democratic institutions, and Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. The Itamaraty deemed the remarks unprecedented and ordered the return of Brazil's ambassador in Buenos Aires for consultations, escalating diplomatic tension following Milei's comments at the PL convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy.

item.title: Governador de Buenos Aires critica Milei por fala sobre governo do Brasil: ‘Vergonha alheia’
item.description: The governor of Buenos Aires, Axel Kicillof, criticized Argentine President Javier Milei's remarks during Brazil's PL national convention, calling them 'foreign shame' for insulting President Lula and the Brazilian government. Kicillof stated Milei does not represent the Argentine people's sentiment and defended regional integration, emphasizing Brazil as Argentina's main trading partner and warning that Milei's comments risk investments, exports, and jobs.

item.title: Zema oficializa candidatura ao Planalto nesta segunda e deixa vice para agosto
item.description: Romeu Zema officially announced his candidacy for President of Brazil during the Novo party’s national convention in Brasília. The vice-presidential pick remains undecided, with ongoing negotiations for political alliances, and Joaquim Barbosa is the primary target. His campaign platform emphasizes public security, privatizations, and criticism of Lula’s foreign policy.

item.title: Quais foram as declarações de Milei que abriram crise com o governo Lula
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei triggered a diplomatic crisis with Brazil after insulting President Lula, calling him a 'prisoner', 'thief', and 'socialist trash', and referring to Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes as 'bald trash', during a speech at the PL convention in São Paulo. The Brazilian government summoned Argentina’s ambassadors in Brasília and Buenos Aires for explanations, condemning the remarks as an unprecedented interference in Brazilian elections and an attack on the dignity of a head of state on their own soil.

item.title: Paraguai e Argentina podem ser entrave para aceleração de acordo entre Mercosul e China, diz especialista em economia chinesa
item.description: Despite a favorable geopolitical moment to accelerate a Mercosul-China agreement, Paraguay and Argentina pose significant obstacles, according to Chinese economy expert Roberto Dumas. Paraguay’s recognition of Taiwan as an independent country is identified as the primary barrier, given China’s sensitivity on the issue.

item.title: O candidato que se sai melhor contra Lula no segundo turno em nova pesquisa
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) performs best against Lula in a hypothetical second-round scenario, with 43% voting intention versus Lula’s 45%, within the poll’s two-point margin of error. Over two weeks, the gap between Lula and Caiado narrowed from nine to two points, showing the most significant shift among tested candidates. In the first round, Lula leads with 42%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 33%, while Caiado trails at 6%.

item.title: A força da marca Bolsonaro e a construção do mito Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro was confirmed as the PL candidate and remains in a runoff position according to Datafolha, despite investigations into the fate of over R$60 million donated by jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro. His campaign promises to implement Zero-Based Budgeting (OBZ), a private-sector management method linked to strict spending cuts. Meanwhile, Lula has retooled his campaign to retell his personal story, aiming to counter the perception among youth that he is 'part of the system', with Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola) serving as the link to the Planalto.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio diz que Bolsonaro não sabia de vídeo com IA exibido na convenção; especialistas apontam riscos jurídicos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign claims the AI-generated video shown at the PL national convention was produced exclusively by their team, without prior knowledge from Jair Bolsonaro, and complied with TSE rules and STF restrictions. The defense relies on the video's initial AI disclosure and its classification as an intraparty act. However, electoral law experts warn the case may be reviewed by electoral justice and could have implications in the STF.

item.title: ‘Interferência externa’: o apoio de Xi Jinping a Lula em meio a pressão de Trump
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping expressed support for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in his opposition to external interference during a phone call amid U.S. tariff pressure under Donald Trump. Lula emphasized accelerating the Mercosul-China trade agreement and reaffirmed his commitment to market diversification, while Trump imposed new tariffs on Brazilian goods, which Lula characterizes as political interference in the election year.

item.title: Eleição será marcada por melhoras nas contas do País, afirma Durigan
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that Lula’s third term will end in 2026 with respect for institutions and improved fiscal indicators. He emphasized that the upcoming election will be marked by progress in public accounts, reflecting the effectiveness of current economic policies.

item.title: Governo Lula é aprovado por 47% e rejeitado por 49%, diz BTG/Nexus
item.description: Lula's government has 47% approval and 49% rejection, according to BTG/Nexus, with slight fluctuation from the previous survey. Approval reaches 62% in the Northeast, while disapproval hits 64% in the South. The margin of error is 2 percentage points.

item.title: China se opõe à interferência externa no Brasil, diz Xi Jinping a Lula
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping reaffirmed China's support for Brazilian sovereignty and opposition to external interference during a call with Lula, emphasizing cooperation in AI, satellites, critical minerals, and fertilizers. The statement comes amid tensions with the U.S., which Lula accused of attempting to discredit Brazil's elections by denying visas to American officials. Both countries also agreed to accelerate a Mercosul-China agreement with necessary flexibilities.

item.title: Convenções inauguram corrida ao Planalto com disputas jurídica, tecnológica e IA
item.description: The 2024 party conventions officially launched the 2026 presidential race, with the PL nominating Flávio Bolsonaro, using an AI-generated representation of Jair Bolsonaro via voice and gestures, and featuring Javier Milei. The event sparked controversy over potential misinformation and initiated a legal debate on synthetic media in campaigns, while the PT prepares to formalize Lula’s candidacy and other parties present Ronaldo Caiado and Romeu Zema.

item.title: Milei não vai pedir desculpas ao Brasil após reclamação de Lula, diz imprensa argentina
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei will not apologize to Brazil after his inflammatory speech in São Paulo, in which he called Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes 'bald trash' and criticized Lula, triggering what Argentine media calls the worst diplomatic crisis between the two nations in 50 years. Brazil summoned ambassadors for explanations but ruled out extreme measures, while Argentine officials confirmed no apology will come from either the ambassador or the president.

item.title: Nexus: Lula se distancia de Flávio entre eleitores “não polarizados”
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll released on January 27 shows President Lula has significantly widened his lead over Senator Flávio Bolsonaro among 'non-polarized' voters — defined as those who do not align with either anti-Lulism or Bolsonarismo. The gap between the two has grown considerably over the past two weeks, indicating a shift in this moderate electorate segment. Lula’s growing advantage suggests he is gaining traction among voters who reject extreme ideological identification.

item.title: Lula nega vistos a EUA por suspeita de ingerência eleitoral
item.description: The Lula administration denied entry visas to two senior U.S. State Department officials, Riley M. Barnes and Samuel Samson, over concerns of foreign interference in Brazil’s electoral process. The move followed a determination by Itamaraty that the officials’ planned mission aimed to undermine confidence in Brazil’s electronic voting system, coinciding with Flávio Bolsonaro’s advocacy for foreign election observers.

item.title: Entenda a briga entre Lula e Milei e como a crise diplomática entre os países escalou
item.description: The diplomatic crisis between Brazil and Argentina escalated after Argentine President Javier Milei called Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a 'prisoner' and 'thief', and insulted Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes during the PL National Convention in São Paulo. The Brazilian government responded by summoning the Argentine ambassador and defending national sovereignty, marking a new low in bilateral relations already strained by ideological differences since Milei took office in December 2023.

item.title: Como a melhora na percepção da economia ajuda Lula na disputa contra Flávio, segundo pesquisa
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows that improved economic perception — with 40% of respondents viewing the economy as better under Lula and a drop in those rating it as bad or terrible from 53% to 49% — coincided with Lula widening his lead over Flávio Bolsonaro. In the first round, Lula’s advantage grew from 6 to 9 points (42% to 33%), and in the runoff simulation, from 3 to 4 points (47% to 43%). This indicates that more positive economic views are bolstering Lula’s electoral standing.

item.title: Pesquisa BTG/Nexus: Lula lidera 1º turno com 42%, Flávio Bolsonaro tem 33%
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leading the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election with 42% of voting intentions, while Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) trails with 33%. The 9-point gap indicates a comfortable advantage for Lula in this initial scenario.

item.title: Brasil convoca embaixador da Argentina após ataques de Milei e eleva crise
item.description: The Brazilian government summoned Argentina's ambassador and recalled its own envoy from Buenos Aires after President Javier Milei attacked President Lula, the Supreme Federal Court, and Brazilian institutions during an event in São Paulo and a subsequent radio interview. The Itamaraty labeled the remarks an 'infamous act' with no precedent, marking one of the strongest diplomatic responses in years, comparable to the 2024 Israel crisis.

item.title: Os planos do governo brasileiro para a visita do presidente da Coreia do Sul, nesta segunda
item.description: President Lula will receive South Korean President Lee Jae Myung for an official visit to Brazil this Monday, accompanied by a delegation of South Korean businessmen interested in deals with Brazil's productive sector. The Brazilian government aims to advance partnerships, particularly in health, with the Ministry of Health seeking to leverage South Korean experience to expand the SUS Smart ICU project, targeting 14 additional units by year-end. The initiative aims to deploy AI technologies for bed management, patient flow, and Samu 192 integration to speed up critical patient assessment before hospital arrival.

item.title: A reação dos EUA após governo Lula negar vistos a dois funcionários de Trump
item.description: The Brazilian government denied entry visas to two high-ranking U.S. State Department officials, Riley M. Barnes and Samuel D. Samson, who planned to discuss freedom of expression in the context of the 2026 elections. The Lula administration stated the visit aimed to cast doubt on the integrity of Brazil’s electoral system, particularly following Flávio Bolsonaro’s recent attacks on electronic voting machines at an event with ambassadors. The Trump administration denied any interference, calling the visit routine and rejecting allegations of election meddling as baseless.

item.title: Ministro da Fazenda diz que Brasil está melhor que a Argentina e chama Milei de 'palhaço'
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that Brazil's economy is better than Argentina's, citing lower country risk, lower unemployment, lower inflation, and a trade surplus. He called Argentine President Javier Milei a 'clown' after Milei attended the launch of Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy and criticized the STF. Durigan emphasized that despite high interest rates, there is no risk of recession in 2027, projecting 2% GDP growth.

item.title: Garotinho empata com Ruas no RJ, aponta Quaest
item.description: Former governor Anthony Garotinho (Republicans) is tied for second place with Douglas Ruas (PL), president of the Alerj, in the race for Rio de Janeiro's governorship, according to a Quaest poll. Both candidates have 10% of first-round voting intentions, with Ruas backed by Flávio Bolsonaro. The survey shows a tight contest for second place in the state.

item.title: Lula e Xi conversam por telefone e discutem acordo do Mercosul com a China
item.description: President Lula spoke by phone with Xi Jinping to discuss deepening Brazil-China partnership, including Mercosul-China trade agreement negotiations, cooperation in high-tech sectors and critical minerals, and shared concerns about global conflicts impacting food and energy security. Both leaders reaffirmed commitment to multilateralism and coordination in the UN, BRICS, and other forums. Lula also criticized recent U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods as a 'strategic mistake'.

item.title: Flávio tem 50% contra 28% de Lula em 2º turno no PR, diz Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll conducted from July 21 to 25, 2026 in Paraná shows Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) leading a hypothetical second-round runoff against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) with 50% of voting intentions, compared to Lula’s 28%. The survey has a 3 percentage point margin of error and a 95% confidence level. Lula is the most rejected candidate in the state, with 68% rejection, and his government is disapproved by 60% of respondents.

item.title: Lula é aprovado por 47% e desaprovado por 49%, diz BTG/Nexus
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll released on July 27, 2026 shows 47% of voters approve and 49% disapprove of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's work, with a margin of error of 2 percentage points. Government evaluation reveals 36% rate his administration as 'excellent' or 'good', 20% as 'fair', and 43% as 'poor' or 'terrible'. The survey was conducted after the U.S. announced a 12.5% surcharge on Brazilian products.

item.title: Após tarifaço de Trump, Lula discute acordo China-Mercosul com Xi Jinping
item.description: Lula and Xi Jinping spoke by phone to discuss deepening bilateral cooperation and accelerating negotiations for a Mercosul-China trade agreement, emphasizing market diversification and the need for flexibility in the deal. The call took place shortly after new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian exports took effect, though the tariffs were not explicitly mentioned as a topic. China’s government highlighted the importance of strengthening strategic coordination and upholding equity in global governance.

item.title: Datafolha: Para 52%, Trump quer ajudar candidatura Flávio à Presidência com tarifaço
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows 52% of Brazilians believe Donald Trump is using increased tariffs on Brazilian goods to aid Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential candidacy. Among Lula voters, this rises to 73%, while 29% of Bolsonaro supporters also share this view. The survey, conducted July 22–23 with 2,004 respondents, has a two-point margin of error.

item.title: Lula tem 47% contra 43% de Flávio no 2º turno, diz BTG/Nexus
item.description: Lula leads Flávio Bolsonaro by 4 percentage points in a hypothetical runoff (47% to 43%), according to BTG/Nexus poll from July 2026. Lula also wins in all other tested scenarios, including the first round (42% to 33%) and against candidates like Zema, Caiado and Renan Santos. The poll shows high rejection for both main candidates (50% for Flávio, 48% for Lula) and a near-even split in government approval (47% approve, 49% disapprove).

item.title: Benedita lidera corrida ao Senado no RJ, diz Quaest
item.description: A Quaest poll released on July 27, 2026, shows Benedita da Silva (PT) leading the Senate race in Rio de Janeiro, though technically tied with Marcelo Criv with Marcelo Crivella (Republicans) within the 3-point margin of error. The survey interviewed 1,200 people from July 21–25, with a 95% confidence level and TSE registration numbers BR-07670/2026 and RJ-02671/2026. The study, funded by Banco Genial, cost R$205,008.84.

item.title: Caiado cresce e empata tecnicamente com Lula no 2º turno, indica Nexus
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll released on Monday shows Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) technically tied with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in a hypothetical second-round matchup. Lula leads numerically with 45% voting intention, while Caiado has 43%, within the poll’s two-point margin of error. The result reflects Caiado’s growth and a competitive scenario in a potential runoff between the two candidates.

item.title: Chanceler brasileiro chama declarações de Milei de “inaceitáveis”
item.description: Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira condemned Argentine President Javier Milei's remarks as rude, vulgar and unacceptable, stating they constituted improper interference in Brazil's domestic affairs. Milei, speaking at the Liberal Party convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy, called President Lula a "prisoner" and Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes "bald trash," triggering a diplomatic rift that prompted Brazil to summon the Argentine ambassador in Brasília and the Brazilian ambassador in Buenos Aires for explanations.

item.title: Datafolha: 52% acreditam que Trump quer ajudar Flávio Bolsonaro com tarifaço
item.description: A Datafolha survey found that 52% of Brazilians believe the tariff imposed by Trump on Brazil aims to support Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential campaign, while 37% reject this idea. Among Lula voters, 73% agree the tariff benefits Bolsonaro, compared to only 29% among Bolsonaro supporters. The poll also shows 34% blame Lula for the trade dispute, 28% blame Trump, and 23% hold the Bolsonaro brothers responsible.

item.title: Lula define ato de abertura da campanha no dia 16 e deve faltar a primeiro debate
item.description: Lula has set the official opening of his reelection campaign for August 16 at the Vila Euclides stadium in São Bernardo do Campo, coinciding with the date of the first Band debate, making his participation in the event highly unlikely. The move aims to highlight his union history in the region and prioritize key electoral colleges and PT-governed Northeastern states in the campaign launch. Campaign allies worry Lula, as the sole left-wing candidate, will be targeted by right-wing opponents, while Band is considering rescheduling the debate to secure his attendance.

item.title: Michelle ficará fora das decisões da campanha Flávio, avaliam aliados
item.description: Allies of Michelle Bolsonaro say that, despite reconciling with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, she will not be involved in the key decisions of his presidential campaign. Her contribution will be limited to recording videos and mobilizing supporters, as she remains focused on caring for her husband, former president Jair Bolsonaro, and potentially running for Senate in the Federal District.

item.title: Michelle, Flávio, Zema e mais: veja as candidaturas ainda com impasses
item.description: As party conventions (July 20 to August 5) are underway, but key pre-candidates like Romeu Zema (Novo), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), and Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) remain undecided on critical aspects: Zema and Flávio are still seeking a running mate, while Michelle is undecided about running for Senate in Brasília. Parties have until August 15 to formally register candidacies after conventions.
